explainer_content.short_definition: A smooth late-1970s/early-1980s studio-pop road of jazz chords, R&B-schooled vocals, elite session playing, and immaculate adult-radio polish.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Yacht rock is a later name for a very specific smooth studio sound. Steely Dan, Michael McDonald-era Doobie Brothers, Christopher Cross, Toto, Kenny Loggins, and related artists make rock feel sleek, harmonically expensive, and rhythmically relaxed.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It turns professionalism into a vibe. The lane is a masterclass in session-player precision, adult-contemporary crossover, blue-eyed soul influence, and pop arrangements where nothing sounds accidental.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The groove is clean, the chords are richer than standard soft rock, and the musicianship is almost invisible because it is so controlled.
what_to_listen_for: Electric piano and clean guitar textures
Smooth backing vocals and blue-eyed soul phrasing
A relaxed but exact drum groove
Studio polish that feels expensive rather than loud
